assessment.why: Full recompute costs ~21% on H200 (H7). FSDP-sharded states take ~52 GB of 141 GB, so un-recomputed activations at 4k/mbs1 likely fit (H5). The 262k-vocab logits are the main risk.
H200 compile gains are large (FSDP2 +24%). HF Trainer graph breaks and recompute interplay will cut this, and HF overhead limits the gain (H6).
Keeps the global batch. Halves FSDP all-gather/reduce-scatter rounds per token and gives larger GEMMs. Comm and glue are a big share of H200 step time (H15). Activations double but are checkpointed.
The 262k vocab makes HF's fp32 logits/CE huge (~10+ GB, slow). Fused linear-CE plus RMSNorm/SwiGLU fusion cut memory and glue time. Unsupported arch mapping is a risk.
Recomputing half the layers recovers about half of the ~21% recompute tax (H7) with a lower memory risk than disabling it. Gives no gain if the harness ignores the kwarg.
Skips the backward all-gather, but keeps ~52 GB of bf16 unsharded params resident on top of ~52 GB of states. NVLink all-gather is mostly overlapped at a ~5 s step, so the gain is small.
About 3.2B sharded params per GPU. Foreach Adam takes tens of ms against a multi-second step, so fusing gains little. DTensor fused-Adam support depends on the torch version.
Mainly reduces fragmentation of the large variable logits buffers. It helps feasibility of no-recompute/mbs2 more than speed.
NVLS accelerates NVSwitch collectives. FSDP comm is mostly overlapped, so disabling it frees a little memory and at most slows comm slightly.
Training is bf16, so almost no fp32 matmuls run on the hot path. TF32 only affects stray fp32 GEMMs.
Steps take seconds for ~8k tokens per GPU. Two workers already hide tokenized data loading.
Input tensors are tiny (token ids) compared with step time. Pinning does not matter.

calls.memory_note: FSDP full-shard leaves ~52 GB/GPU for fp32 params, grads and Adam states, plus ~10-13 GB for 262k-vocab fp32 logits without Liger, so ~60-70 GB remains for activations; that should cover disabling recompute at mbs1/4k but not with mbs2 or no-reshard stacked on top.

findings.issue: Compute (3099 ms, 91.7%) runs eagerly. Element-wise work is unfused: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE and residual adds each launch separate kernels in forward and again in the checkpointed recompute.

The HF causal-LM loss materializes full logits (4096 x ~151k), upcasts them to fp32 for cross-entropy and keeps them for backward. That is large memory traffic and a large allocation on every micro-batch. Liger's fused kernels (fused linear cross-entropy, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE) remove it.

Full activation recompute on every layer (every_n_layers=1) re-runs the whole forward in backward, roughly a third of compute. With 141 GiB per GPU and a 1.7B model at seq 4096, batch 1, recompute can likely be reduced or turned off. Batch 2 with grad-accum 1 also keeps global_batch at 16 while givi
The optimizer step (61.6 ms) uses the non-fused AdamW in for-each mode, with several kernel passes over the parameters.
FSDP2 reshards after forward, so with grad-accum 2 and recompute the all-gathers run again in backward and on every micro-batch. Comm is 71 ms, mostly hidden.
Each update allocates and frees new activation and logit buffers of varying size, which can fragment the caching allocator and cause cudaMalloc retries or cache flushes.

hypotheses.mechanism: fewer, larger micro-batches: per_device_train_batch_size 2 with gradient_accumulation_steps 1 (global batch stays 8x2x1=16); halves the FSDP all-gather/reduce-scatter rounds and per-micro-batch launch
hypotheses.rationale: With reshard on and GA=2, every update does two forward+backward passes, each with full parameter all-gathers. For a 25.8B model that traffic is large, and most of it is probably hidden inside the 3.1 s compute phase. MBS2 doubles activations (+13 GiB) and logits (+6 GiB), which fits the 67 GiB margin. Glue-kernel and launch overhead also amortizes over twice the tokens.

hypotheses.mechanism: selective recompute: checkpoint every 2nd layer instead of every layer (removes about half of the recompute forward)
hypotheses.rationale: Compute is 92% of the update. Full recompute costs about 20% on H200 (rule H7), so recomputing half the layers should recover roughly 8-11%. Stored activations for 15 extra layers at seq 4096 and MBS1 should fit in the 67 GiB margin.

hypotheses.mechanism: selective recompute: checkpoint every 4th layer (removes about 3/4 of the recompute)
hypotheses.rationale: This recovers most of the about 20% full-recompute tax while keeping some checkpointing as a memory guard, a fallback if fully disabling recompute (queued) OOMs. Activation growth is roughly 3/4 of a no-recompute run. That is close to the margin, so OOM risk is moderate.

hypotheses.mechanism: selective recompute: checkpoint every 3rd layer
hypotheses.rationale: An intermediate point between every 2 and every 4 layers. It removes about 2/3 of the recompute forward, which is a large saving in a compute-dominated update, and keeps memory below the every-4 setting.

hypotheses.mechanism: FSDP2 without reshard after forward (fsdp_v2_noreshard.json): keep gathered parameters from forward to backward, removing the backward all-gather per micro-batch
hypotheses.rationale: With GA=2 there are 4 parameter all-gathers per update (fwd and bwd per micro-batch). Skipping the backward re-gather cuts gather traffic and the stream synchronization around it. The exposed comm is only 2%, but gathers also delay compute through dependencies. The cost is that unsharded bf16 parameters of up to about 45 GiB stay resident, close to the margin.

hypotheses.mechanism: expandable_segments allocator: avoids fragmentation, cudaMalloc retries and cache flushes with variable-size FSDP/recompute buffers

Amortizes the AdamW step over 2 microbatches per token. The step is short next to a ~5-6 s compute step. It doubles the global batch, so the job may reject it.
Fuses elementwise ops around the GEMMs. Risks: graph breaks with FSDP2 plus checkpointing, and caches on a shared filesystem racing across 2 hosts.

assessment.why: 248k vocab x 4096 tokens: fused linear-CE avoids materializing ~1B logits, saving GBs and time; RMSNorm/SwiGLU fusions help. Risk: model type may lack a Liger patch, then it is a no-op.
Halves FSDP all-gathers per token and per-step overhead on fast H100 compute. Doubles activations and logits, so OOM risk at 77 GiB. Also doubles the global batch.
Fuses elementwise and norm ops on a compute-bound H100. HF Trainer with FSDP2 compile can graph-break or fail. Compile warm-up must be kept out of the timing.
Skips the backward all-gather, but holds ~18 GB of unsharded bf16 params. 80GB H100 (vs 95/141 GB in nearest envs) makes OOM likely without activation checkpointing.
Single fused kernel for ~1.1B sharded params per rank. The step is a small share of a ~1 s+ compute step, so gain is small. DTensor support needed (recent torch).
Reduces fragmentation and the risk of allocator retries near the 77 GiB limit. Not a throughput lever unless memory is tight.
Training matmuls run in bf16 under mixed precision. Few fp32 GEMMs remain for TF32 to accelerate.
Pre-tokenized LM data at 1 sample per micro-step is cheap. Two workers already keep up with a ~1 s step.
The host-to-device copy of a 4096-token id tensor is negligible either way.
H100 SXM NVSwitch supports NVLS. Disabling it frees a little memory but makes FSDP collectives use more SMs. Comm is mostly overlapped, so the effect is near zero.
An optimizer step every micro-batch doubles optimizer cost per token. FSDP still reduce-scatters every micro-step, so nothing is saved. Halves the global batch.

calls.memory_note: Per rank, FSDP-sharded fp32 params, grads and Adam state take ~18 GB, plus seq-4096 activations (unknown whether checkpointing is on) and ~8-12 GB for 248k-vocab logits; that leaves modest headroom on 77.3 GiB, so mbs 2 or no-reshard may OOM unless Liger's fused CE frees the logit memory.
